project_scope.note: Genus-level processing is complete without promoting reviewed HOLD or FAIL taxa. Canonical learner pages remain limited to the three installed PASS species.

study_strategy.warning: Do not identify Passiflora from flower color alone. San Antonio-area records are especially vulnerable to confusion between native P. foetida and introduced P. lanuginosa/ciliata-type plants; use leaf/bract/fruit morphology plus provenance.

quick_split: P. affinis — canonical PASS; broad cowboy-hat leaves, floral bracts present, greenish-yellow flower, purple-black berry.
P. lutea — canonical PASS; glandless petiole, broad rounded entire 3-lobed leaves, tiny green-yellow flower and small berry.
P. tenuiloba — canonical PASS; paired cuplike petiole glands and extremely narrow deeply divided birdwing leaves; tiny green petal-less-looking flower.
P. incarnata — reviewed range HOLD; paired petiole glands, large broad serrate 3-lobed leaves, enormous purple/white corona flower, large maypop fruit.
P. foetida — reviewed range HOLD; densely hairy fetid foliage, finely divided sticky bract cage, pale flower with purple-blue corona, greenish mature fruit.
P. lanuginosa — reviewed target-zone FAIL; introduced Mexico–Guatemala lookalike with darker angular leaves, pinker flowers, and smooth red fruit.
